subject: Post-demo: clarify procurement route (card vs PO) and SOC2/DPA next steps
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@nexwell.com>, Daren Liu <daren.liu@consultingpartners.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: clarify procurement route (card vs PO) and SOC2/DPA next steps

Hi Aisha / Daren —

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying Qs to unblock procurement: 

- Commercial paths we discussed:
  * Quick pilot (credit card) — up to $X in monthly spend, immediate onboarding via hosted API.
  * PO/contract — required for committed spend and enterprise terms (SLA, custom data protections).
  * Marketplace procurement — possible through the cloud marketplace but often requires a separate reseller/marketplace contract and adds lead time.

Action items for your team: can you confirm which path Procurement prefers for an initial 3-month evaluation? Also, is there an internal threshold for when a PO is mandatory vs card?

Security/compliance gating: you asked for SOC 2 and DPA — attaching the SOC2 summary and our standard DPA draft. If you want a signed DPA, we can route that through legal once commercial terms are aligned.

Attachments: SOC2-Report-Redwood-2025.pdf (summary), Redwood-DPA-2026.docx (draft)

Next steps I propose:
1) If card pilot: we provide an invoiceable card flow and a payment link; we'll set up a scoped project with clear success metrics.
2) If PO route: Ben will share typical lead times and draft commercial language; Marissa to approve any non-standard discount.
3) Security questionnaire: if you have a questionnaire, please share; we can have our security team complete it — typical turnaround 3–5 business days for standard questionnaires.

Cc'ing Ben to confirm pricing thresholds and Marissa for approvals.

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for the clear summary. A couple of clarifying questions from Procurement:

1) For the pilot, would Redwood accept a company card for charges up to $15k per month, or do you require a PO for any pilot of that size?
2) If we go the PO route, what is the expected lead time from signature to being live?
3) Marketplace: we're interested if it reduces internal procurement friction — is Redwood available via the AWS Marketplace or GCP Marketplace?

We will also need SOC2 and DPA to be submitted to InfoSec for review. If you can attach those, that will help move things faster. Finally, we have a security questionnaire that we'd like Redwood to complete; can you confirm the contact for that?

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@nexwell.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: clarify procurement route (card vs PO) and SOC2/DPA next steps

Hi Aisha —

Answers inline: 

1) Card vs PO threshold: for most customers we allow credit card payments for short pilots up to $10k/month under standard terms. For a pilot up to $15k/month we can make an exception if we lock a 3-month pilot agreement (card-authorized) and add basic usage caps. If Procurement prefers a PO, we'll of course accommodate that.

2) PO lead time: once legal/commercial redlines are agreed, typical PO-to-production time is 7–14 business days (depends on signature flow).

3) Marketplace: Redwood is currently listed on AWS Marketplace (metered and subscription options) and in discussions for GCP Marketplace — AWS Marketplace is the fastest marketplace option today. Marketplace purchases may require additional reseller terms and a 2–3 week setup.

I've attached the SOC2 summary and our DPA draft to this message (same files referenced earlier). For the security questionnaire, please send the template to security@redwood.ai; our security team (Led by person on that alias) will pick it up and return a completed version within 3–5 business days for standard questionnaires.

Ben / Marissa — can you confirm if a 3-month card-authorized pilot up to $15k/month is acceptable from a commercial/discount perspective? If not, what commit level would you prefer we ask for?

Attachments: SOC2-Report-Redwood-2025.pdf, Redwood-DPA-2026.docx

Thanks,
Sofia

---

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: clarify procurement route (card vs PO) and SOC2/DPA next steps

Sofia —

I'm fine with a 3-month pilot on card up to $15k/month with the following guardrails:
- No custom SLA or discounts beyond standard pilot terms.
- We capture success metrics (API latency, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens) in the MOP/SOW.
- Escalation point to Rishi if we need extended credit terms or a longer commit.

If Procurement insists on PO, typical ask is at least a 6-month commit to justify discounting. Marissa — please chime in if you want to limit the pilot cap or require a minimum ARR to approve any discount.

Ben Carter
